```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)

```

```{r growth curves}

#read in input data extracted from spreadsheets
cleaned_input <- read.csv("../inputs/cleandf_params.csv")

#calculate aboveground carbon as a function of tree taxon and age class
chapman_richards <- function(A, k, p, age){
  agc <- A * (1 - exp(-k * age))^p
  return(agc)
}

#calculate growth rate per age class
agc_rate <- function(agc, age){
  rate_out <- agc / age
  return(rate_out)
}

#run examples
# NOTE - it will take an extra step but we can do custom "n" per species in the future
test_group <- "Pseudotsuga"
n_age_classes <- 150
n_species <- length(unique(cleaned_input$group))

#select relevant columns and add 'p' parameter
growth_params <- cleaned_input %>%
  select(group, A, k) %>%
  mutate(p = 2) # NOTE - double check what p is - expansion of plantation or something else?

#run AGC and rate functions per age class per species
age_classes <- do.call("rbind", replicate(n_age_classes + 1, growth_params, simplify = FALSE)) %>%
  arrange(group) %>%
  mutate(age = rep(seq(from = 0, to = n_age_classes), times = n_species)) %>%
  mutate(agc = chapman_richards(A, k, p, age)) %>%
  mutate(agc_rate = agc_rate(agc, age)) %>%
  mutate(agc_rate = ifelse(is.nan(agc_rate), 0, agc_rate))

#quick test plot
ggplot(age_classes) +
  geom_line(aes(x = age, y = agc)) +
  facet_wrap(facets = vars(group))

#TODO - ask Jacob where this growth data comes from

```

```{r}

#set species parameters
#eventually it would be nice to have the actual rotation age formulas in here
#rather than hard-coding everything

tmp_group <- "Pseudotsuga"
faustmann <- 30
msy <- 54
total_area <- 100000
area_per_age <- total_area / faustmann
sim_years <- 200

#pare down age class dataset
dougfir_agc <- age_classes %>%
  filter(group == tmp_group) %>%
  select(group, age, agc)

#simulation under faustmann rotation age (economic)
#each year should be the same as the faustmann-aged areas are just converted back to 1-year areas
table_faustmann <- tibble(group = tmp_group,
                          sim_year = rep(1:sim_years, each = faustmann + 1),
                          age = rep(0:faustmann, times = sim_years),
                          area = area_per_age,
                          scenario = "faustmann") 

#simulation under msy rotation age (biological)
#max age in the system will start at faustmann and then increase to MSY
max_age <- faustmann
age_classes_tmp <- 0:faustmann
age_classes_all <- c()
sim_years_all <- c()

#for loop to figure out age classes per year
#there's definitely a cleaner way of doing this but i am lazy
for (i in 1:sim_years){
    
  #add years and age classes to lists
  age_classes_all <- c(age_classes_all, age_classes_tmp)
  sim_years_all <- c(sim_years_all, rep(i, times = length(age_classes_tmp)))
  
  if (max_age < (msy - 1)){ #latent period - letting trees grow up to MSY
    
    #age up trees by one year
    age_classes_tmp <- age_classes_tmp + 1
    
    #increase max_age by one
    max_age <- max_age + 1
    
  } else{ #harvest period - oldest trees have reached MSY
    
    #cut down oldest trees
    age_classes_tmp[age_classes_tmp == msy] <- 0
    
  }
}

#simulation under msy rotation age (biological)
table_msy <- tibble(group = tmp_group,
                    sim_year = sim_years_all,
                    age = age_classes_all,
                    area = area_per_age,
                    scenario = "msy") 

#combine scenario datasets
all_scenarios <- bind_rows(table_faustmann, table_msy) %>%
  left_join(dougfir_agc) %>% 
  mutate(agc_area = area_per_age * agc) #is this right? AGC x area?

#get annual carbon sums per scenario
all_scenarios_yearly <- all_scenarios %>%
  group_by(sim_year, scenario) %>%
  summarize(agc_sum = sum(agc_area))

#test plot
ggplot(all_scenarios_yearly) +
  geom_line(aes(x = sim_year, y = agc_sum, color = scenario))

#how much unmanaged forest would you be saving?
  #see herbicide study for example

```
